memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Celebrate this as a festival to the LORD for seven days each year.
This is to be a lasting ordinance for the generations to come;
celebrate it in the seventh month. Live in temporary shelters for
seven days: All native-born Israelites are to live in such shelters so
your descendants will know that I had the Israelites live in temporary
shelters when I brought them out of Egypt. I am the LORD your God'"
- Lev 23:41-43 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the reason God gives for the whole exercise: so your
descendants will know. The shelters were a teaching tool. A child would
sleep under leaves, look up at the stars through the gaps, and ask,
"Why are we doing this?" And a parent would answer with the story of
the exodus.

Faith was passed down through shared experience, not just instruction.
The children did not merely hear about the wilderness; for a week each
year, they tasted it.

Dear friend, this is a challenge to every parent, grandparent, uncle,
aunt and church worker. What are the children around you actually
experiencing of your faith? Not just what they are told, but what they
see, join in and remember.

Moses urged Israel to impress God's commands on their children - to
talk about them at home, on the road, at bedtime and in the morning
(Deut 6:6-7). Paul reminded Timothy of the sincere faith that lived
first in his grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice (2 Tim 1:5).

You may not have a festival calendar. But you have meals, journeys,
bedtimes and ordinary days.

Make some of them memorable for God's sake.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What are the children in my life learning about God by watching me?
2. What family or church practice could make faith memorable for them?
3. Whose faith shaped mine, and have I thanked God for them?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, help me pass on a living faith to the next generation - not
just words, but a life they can see and remember. Amen.
